items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: I said, "Hey Herman, look, why don't you try this.

ctx.x: Billy Muir had written out some parts for me to play and for himself to play, and Alan to play -- and we were trying to overdub to these tapes that Perez Parado had done out in California - and one of the tunes was "Patricia" that we were trying to do.

So we were getting ready to call the date off because it wasn't making it, and Herman was a little let down and everything, and I got the bright idea -- I said, "Hey Herman, look, why don't you try this. Let Alan Hannon play what he's playing on the base guitar, let Billy Muir play this rhythm on the tambourine" -- and I played the rhythm for him that I wanted him to play on the tambourine, which I still have that tambourine -- I saved that tambourine. "And I'll play straight eights with a backbeat on the drum…
So they ran the tape, and we played 8 bars -- and Herman said, "Let's make it" and it became a hit for Perez Parado and it saved his job, too.
